items.title: 73243_Joe Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Walter Johnson, John Kirby and Horace Henderson.

ctx.x: Fletcher Henderson's house. (something about Russell Lewis and Joe's brother, first trumpet player with the band) So this particular day I was pretty good chops ... and that was, a lot of good guys in the band you might remember... brass section, Russell, Red and me, Russell playing first, I was playing second and Red was playing third. Hilton Jefferson playing first alto, Procope, Buster Bailey, Coleman Hawkins, Russell Toco (?) ... Walter Johnson, John Kirby and Horace Henderson.
And the trombones were who, Claude?

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: I brought him out of Columbus, Ohio. And he had an alto. I immediately put him (inaudible) on tenor, because he had such a drive. what he did for the Lunceford band.

ctx.x: Yeah, they list only one. Who was the other?

A guy named Joe Thomas was the great tenor saxophonist, with Jimmie Lunceford was the great (inaudible) band. I brought him out of Columbus, Ohio. And he had an alto. I immediately put him (inaudible) on tenor, because he had such a drive. what he did for the Lunceford band. Of course, you know the particular bunch of (inaudible).
